drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Counsel: Subject to our client’s approval, the revised draft reflects your proposed salary, executive-level benefits, and 24-month severance framework, and replaces the post-employment non-compete with limited confidentiality and trade-secret protections. We have proposed a good-reason definition and notice-and-cure procedure for discussion. The Executive’s legal name and governing law remain open pending confirmation of residence and principal work location. All terms remain subject to final agreement and execution.

edits.text: 2. COMPENSATION. The Executive shall receive an annual base salary of $500,000, payable in accordance with the Company’s regular payroll practices, and shall be eligible to participate in employee benefit plans made available to similarly situated senior executives, subject to the applicable plan terms.

3. SEVERANCE. If the Company terminates the Executive’s employment without Cause or the Executive resigns for Good Reason, the Company shall pay the Executive an amount equal to 24 months of the Executive’s then-current base salary, in installments over 24 months in accordance with regular payroll practices, commencing within 30 days after termination, except to the extent a delay is required by applicable law. The Company shall also provide continued health coverage for the Executive and eligible dependents for 24 months on substantially the same terms, including the Executive’s contribution, as immediately before termination, subject to applicable law and plan terms. If continued participation is unavailable, the Company shall provide an economically equivalent, lawful benefit. “Cause” means serious, willful misconduct by the Executive in connection with employment that materially harms the Company; good-faith errors in judgment or ordinary negligence do not constitute Cause. “Good Reason” means, without the Executive’s written consent, a material reduction in base salary, a material diminution in duties or authority, or a material breach of this Agreement by the Company. Good Reason requires written notice within 90 days after the Executive becomes aware of the condition, a 30-day opportunity for the Company to cure, and resignation within 30 days after expiration of the cure period if the condition remains uncured.

4. CONFIDENTIALITY AND TRADE SECRETS. No post-employment non-compete shall apply. The Executive shall not use or disclose the Company’s confidential information except in performing duties for the Company or as permitted by law. Confidential information excludes information that becomes public through no breach by the Executive, was lawfully known to the Executive without restriction, is independently developed without use of confidential information, or is lawfully received from a third party without a duty of confidentiality. This obligation applies only while the information remains confidential; trade secrets remain protected for so long as they qualify as trade secrets under applicable law. Nothing in this Agreement restricts the Executive’s general skills, knowledge, or experience, lawful reporting to or communications with government agencies, protected whistleblowing, or disclosures required by law. Under 18 U.S.C. § 1833(b), the Executive shall not be held criminally or civilly liable under federal or state trade-secret law for a trade-secret disclosure made in confidence to a government official or an attorney solely to report or investigate a suspected violation of law, or made in a complaint or other document filed under seal in a proceeding. In a retaliation action for reporting a suspected violation of law, the Executive may disclose trade secrets to counsel and use them in the proceeding if filings containing them are under seal and disclosure is otherwise made only pursuant to court order.

5. GOVERNING LAW. [To be agreed after confirmation of the Executive’s residence and principal work location.]

receiver.message_back: Subject to our client’s approval and execution, the revised economics and removal of the non-compete are acceptable in principle, provided severance is calculated using base salary before any reduction giving rise to Good Reason, is not subject to mitigation, offset, or a release condition, and Cause requires written particulars and a reasonable opportunity to cure where curable. Please also include a material diminution in executive benefits or a required relocation exceeding 50 miles as Good Reason, extend the post-cure resignation window to 60 days, and leave the Executive’s name and governing law open pending confirmation.
